# Rybbit source attribution

The native General tab's Public Analytics privacy row and share/export controls are adapted to a property-scoped SQLite public flag. Public dashboard navigation retains Rybbit's report pages and sidebar while removing workspace management controls for anonymous visitors. The GA4 gateway applies read-only public guards independently of private links and widget publishing. These adaptations retain Rybbit's AGPL-3.0-only license and attribution.

The entire Rybbit client source tree, shared source and message catalogs were copied from the local Rybbit repository at commit `9cee0e9007ecb574533a4a2f28623b78f84b18a1` (https://github.com/rybbit-io/rybbit), into `frontend/rybbit/`. Original asset folders were copied into `public/`.

The GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 is preserved in `RYBBIT-LICENSE.md`. MIT notices for interior.dev adaptations remain beside their source. `upstream.json` records the SHA256 of every original source file. `adaptations.json` records the locally modified files; `node scripts/rybbit-source.js` checks both lists.

Rybbit's native `server/src/services/favicon/favicon.ts` and `server/src/lib/publicHttpFetch.ts` are also copied into `controllers/rybbitFavicon.ts` and `controllers/publicHttpFetch.ts`, with an Fastify endpoint in `controllers/favicons.js`. Their upstream and adapted SHA256 hashes are recorded in `server-upstream.json`; the service uses the host application's debug logger. `controllers/faviconDns.ts` resolves synthetic proxy DNS answers over HTTPS before the original public-address validation and connection pinning.

The favicon service additionally tries Google's cached favicon after native discovery, with a separate five-second deadline so a slow homepage cannot exhaust the fallback. When a subdomain has no icon, it falls back to its registrable main domain using `tldts` public and private suffix boundaries, sharing the main domain's cached result and expiry. The HTTP transport permits up to 64 KiB of response headers for Google sites' large CSP policies. Native byte limits, image signature checks, public-address restrictions, DNS pinning, cache lifetimes and concurrency queue remain in use.

Native analytics pages, Sankey, retention grid, tables, buttons, icons (Lucide), tooltips, sheets, date controls, chart theme, CSS tokens, sidebar primitives and logo are reused directly. Native Next.js imports are bridged by `frontend/adapter/` to the Fastify/Vite runtime. Adaptations connect GA4 aggregates, retain the original account, organization and team controls, and omit unsupported collector surfaces and the Documentation menu. The rail and navigation retain Rybbit's styling with GA4 destinations. Home, Sites, Globe, API quota, connection and the complete GA4 report catalog are composed from the same imported components. The globe renderer preserves the original GA4 MapLibre/D3 engines and approved India-POV boundaries.

The native Button's `accent` and `success` variants share MetriBee's bee-yellow primary-button tokens with dark text in both themes. Other semantic colors and native button behavior are preserved under the same AGPL-3.0-only license.

The Connection page links to the public MetriBee source repository at https://github.com/nexmoe/MetriBee. Application source archives are not generated or served by the running application.

Rybbit's visitor iframe renderer (`client/src/app/widget/[siteId]/route.ts`) is adapted to Fastify in `controllers/rybbitWidget.ts`, preserving its card/inline markup, styles and refresh behavior with MetriBee branding for existing iframe URLs. Its source hashes are recorded in `server-upstream.json`. Imported `EmbedTab` and `DashboardEmbedTab` sources are retained, while the application exposes one standalone Widgets page using the custom builder and native code-copy controls. Settings are stored locally; Google Analytics remains read-only.

`ConfigurationEditorLayout` is extracted from Rybbit's `FunnelForm` and shared by the existing funnel editor and the custom metric widget editor. Generic widgets reuse Rybbit's `StatBand`, `Delta`, `SiteSessionChart`, controls, theme and code-copy UI. Optional transparent cells and chart colors/value formatters preserve those components' existing defaults. Widget definitions follow the funnel store's property-scoped, serialized, atomic save/edit/delete pattern and live alongside the other embed settings.

The analytics query adapters opt historical reports into TanStack Query session persistence. Native page, journey, retention, event and section components retain their last successful results during background refresh failures; section loading indicators allow interaction with cached rows. These adaptations retain Rybbit's AGPL-3.0-only license.

Analytics query hooks also recheck server-side background report refreshes with a bounded polling interval, replacing stale results when the shared refresh completes. Report freshness preserves original fetch times throughout revalidation.

The native Funnels page loads current and comparison figures independently, reuses shared ordered GA4 report caches, and preserves successful rows when part of a summary fails. Funnel hooks, stat bands and retry controls retain Rybbit's AGPL-3.0-only license and native components.

The Journey page restores the local Rybbit reference's default four steps, two-to-ten depth controls, session statistics, per-step filters, pinned details, paths table, session sheet and funnel dialog. Its hooks select an explicitly ordered-session source, with total sessions and top entry derived from the same population. GA4-only connections open the existing page-transitions report directly; native session journeys are shown only when an ordered source is available, with synthetic demo events clearly labelled. The optional GA4 BigQuery export adapter applies those same native shaping semantics to real event exports and retains the native page, session sheet and controls. The GA4 page-transitions report retains page-view units through an optional Sankey measurement prop. Chinese adapter messages supplement the imported catalogs. `controllers/sessionJourneys.js` adapts the ordered-session shaping, section grouping, end-page truncation, summary and exact session-membership semantics from Rybbit's `server/src/api/analytics/journeyPaths.ts`, `getJourneys.ts`, `getJourneySummary.ts` and `getJourneySessions.ts` at the recorded upstream commit. These adaptations retain Rybbit's AGPL-3.0-only license and attribution.

The native `VersionCheck` notification retains Rybbit's per-tab session check, silent failure and ten-second dismissible update prompt. Its MetriBee adapter reads the root application version and the public `nexmoe/MetriBee` GitHub latest-release endpoint, with the update action linking to the matching release. It is mounted only in the workspace, outside shared and embedded views. This adaptation retains Rybbit's AGPL-3.0-only license and attribution.

MetriBee reuses Rybbit’s 12 next-intl message catalogs, ICU message formatting, native language selector and three-column footer. The footer uses MetriBee branding, project links and the application version. URL locale routing, shared-link preservation, HTML language metadata and supplemental MetriBee translations are local adaptations; no language cookie or account preference is stored. These changes retain the Rybbit AGPL-3.0-only license.

The Footer restores the reference's 1100px content width, 140px logo slot, support-action block and bottom-bar alignment. Its support action links to the MetriBee repository for starring; unavailable upstream marketing, community and legal destinations are omitted. SiteSettings restores the native 1000px desktop dialog, 220px navigation rail, General-tab fields and settings sections, and organization-move confirmation. GA4 name/domain fields are read-only; unsupported collector, import and deletion controls are omitted, and Widgets remains standalone. The small-screen dialog stacks its navigation above the content. Legacy Property access URLs open this dialog on Analytics. These adaptations retain AGPL-3.0-only attribution.

Rybbit's Better Auth client, five organization roles, scope taxonomy, organization/member/team settings, account forms, API-key managers, invitation/reset/consent/transfer pages and user-administration components are reused for the SQLite user system. `lib/permissions.js` and `lib/scopes.js` are compiled from the shared sources; `lib/oauth.mjs` adapts `server/src/lib/oauth.ts` to the MetriBee MCP resource. SQLite-backed access resolution preserves additive member/team grants and per-site role raises. Account, organization, teams, admin, login and signup reuse the complete native pages and layouts, including the original settings rail/user menu (`AccountSidebar.tsx`), administrator tab order, two-column login and signup steps. The decorative login globe uses the approved local India POV boundaries; SQLite database content uses the original admin panels/stat strips. Signup retains the original two-step layout with workspace naming in place of domain/collector setup. GA4 properties remain synchronized by the server; signup does not claim or move properties. Authentication pages remain readable independently of the saved dashboard privacy preference. All retain AGPL-3.0-only attribution.

Saved segments, annotations, Goals and custom Dashboards retain Rybbit’s native React pages, editors, chart interactions and grid layouts. The GA4 card-query builder, presets and aggregate conversion adapters replace collector-specific data access. `frontend/third-party/rybbit-reports/` preserves original PDF and email template sources from the same recorded upstream revision; `lib/reports/templates/` contains their JavaScript adaptations with MetriBee branding and local PDF assets. All imported code and adaptations remain AGPL-3.0-only with Rybbit attribution.

MCP organization/member/team tools in `mcp-server/lib/accountTools.js` adapt Rybbit’s `server/src/mcp/tools/organizations.ts` and the `list_sites` discovery contract from `tools/sites.ts`. The in-process REST bridge and one-use credential-bound verification handoff follow Rybbit’s MCP API client and bearer handoff design. Native personal/organization API-key managers, the scope picker and OAuth consent UI are retained. Adaptations use SQLite and preserve the GA4 analysis tools, scopes and quota guards; both `/api/mcp` and legacy `/mcp` remain supported. AGPL-3.0-only; original authors and license retained.

The account page adds a small MCP connection section next to the native API-key manager. It composes Rybbit’s Ledger, Dialog, Tabs, CodeSnippet and CopyButton components; the original account layout and authorization UI are retained.

Rybbit's native Billing layout, PlanSection, Ledger rows/table, settings navigation and dialogs are adapted in `frontend/adapter/accounts/Billing.tsx` for organization-based Waffo Pancake subscriptions. Standard/Pro prices come from a SQLite catalog rather than Rybbit's event tiers. Checkout, plan changes, billing details and invoice downloads use Waffo-hosted pages; Stripe SDKs are removed. Cloud signup retains the original account/setup steps, then opens organization billing. These changes retain Rybbit's AGPL-3.0-only license and attribution.

The Waffo billing adapter additionally restores Rybbit's native `PlanRow` and monthly/annual dialog composition, `InvoicesSection` table and three-step `CancellationDialog` (reason, alternative, confirmation). Only provider data/actions, fixed organization prices, unavailable Rybbit-specific support/collector promises and MetriBee design-token radii are adapted. Annual amounts remain explicit; invoice numbers remain unknown when Waffo has not supplied them, and invoice actions open the authenticated Waffo portal. The normal billing page no longer includes the sandbox checkout tool. These source adaptations retain AGPL-3.0-only attribution.
